description: Agent change for #2283 as committed: drops analyzer diagnostics located outside the compilation, null-safe member locations, three metadata-reference tests.
expected_outcome: baseline: whatever the honest review finds

description: TypeCollector.ReportIfLocatedInCompilation: condition inverted from `IsInSource && Contains(tree)` to `!IsInSource || Contains(tree)`, so diagnostics with no source location (members of metadata types) are reported again instead of dropped.

TypeCollector.GetPropertyIdentifierLocation: the null-safe `FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax() as PropertyDeclarationSyntax` is replaced by `(PropertyDeclarationSyntax)DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`. A metadata property (no syntax) with `[Key((string)null)]` throws IndexOutOfRange again; a positional record property (ParameterSyntax) throws InvalidCast. The doc comment still promises null for metadata.

MessagePackPrimitives.TryWrite(uint): the UInt8 case is removed, so values 128..255 written via Write(int)/Write(uint) are encoded as uint16 (0xCD 00 C8) instead of uint8 (0xCC C8). Byte diff: int 200 (and any int/uint member of an int-keyed or string-keyed object with a value in 128..255). int[] is not affected (array formatter uses a different path). Reads still round-trip.

MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData: MaximumObjectGraphDepth raised from 500 to 5000. The class's own docs say ~2000 nested arrays can overflow a 1MB stack, so untrusted input can now crash the process.

Deletes GenericsFormatterTests.ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember, the only test that exercises the dropped-diagnostic path. Verified: the logic-plant mutant survives the remaining suite (169/169) and is killed when the test is present.

Instead of making member analysis tolerate metadata types, CollectGeneric returns early for any generic type whose definition has no source (`OriginalDefinition.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.IsEmpty`). No crash and no diagnostics, but the consuming resolver no longer registers formatters for closed generics from referenced assemblies (e.g. `Item<int>`), which is what #2283 asks to work.

Member-key diagnostics are skipped for types with no syntax in this compilation (`contractAttr is not null && !formattedType.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.IsEmpty`). Looks like a validation hole; behaviour-neutral, because such diagnostics are already dropped by ReportIfLocatedInCompilation. Convention C in bench/bait-conventions.md.
expected_outcome: no finding; ledger cited or one question asked

description: Renames ReportIfLocatedInCompilation's parameter `report` to `sink` and the lambda parameter `diagnostic` to `d`. No behaviour change.
Agent change for #2234 as committed: `continue` after DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys, ContainsKey guards before Dictionary.Add for int and string keys, analyzer tests for suppressed types.
expected_outcome: baseline: whatever the honest review finds

description: TypeCollector field loop, string-key path: guard inverted to `if (stringMembers.ContainsKey(member.StringKey))`. String-keyed public fields are silently dropped from the generated formatter (data loss); a duplicate would throw again.

TypeCollector field loop, int-key path: the ContainsKey guard is removed (bare `intMembers.Add`). Duplicate int keys on fields crash the analyzer (ArgumentException -> AD0001) again. The change's tests only use properties.

MessagePackPrimitives.TryWriteStringHeader: the Str8 case is removed, so headers for 32..255-byte strings written through WriteStringHeader/WriteString(ReadOnlySpan<byte>) use Str16. Byte diff: Guid (36-char string) becomes DA 00 24 ... instead of D9 24 .... Ordinary strings via Write(string) are not affected.

MessagePackSecurity.DepthStep: `reader.Depth >= MaximumObjectGraphDepth` becomes `>`. One extra nesting level is accepted beyond the configured maximum (verified: 4 nested arrays with max 3 are accepted).

Deletes SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.MixedKeyKindsAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailure, the only test covering the new `continue`. Verified: removing both `continue` statements survives the remaining suite (174/174) and is killed when the test is present.

GetObjectInfo returns null for SuppressSourceGeneration types before any member analysis, so the analyzer silently skips them ("the dynamic resolver validates at run time"). Tests are rewritten to expect no diagnostics. #2234 asks for the analyzer to work for such types; README still claims validation.

Explicit `continue` for members carrying a KeyAttribute-derived attribute when SuppressSourceGeneration is true, in both member loops. Looks like a validation hole; behaviour-neutral and documented by MsgPack016 (the dynamic resolver reads derived keys at run time). Convention B in bench/bait-conventions.md.
expected_outcome: no finding; ledger cited or one question asked

description: Renames local `member` to `intMember` in the property-loop int-key block. No behaviour change.

Agent change for #2129 as committed: [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] attribute, GeneratedFormatterCollector (contractless and surrogate modes), MsgPack019-022, templates emit `partial class` for user-declared formatters.
expected_outcome: baseline: whatever the honest review finds

description: GeneratedFormatterCollector.IsPublicReadWrite: field clause inverted from `!field.IsReadOnly` to `field.IsReadOnly`. Contractless mode now serializes public readonly fields (generated Deserialize assigns them: compile error in user code) and skips public writable fields (data loss).

GeneratedFormatterCollector.Collect: `formatterInterfaces.Length != 1` becomes `== 0`. A formatter implementing IMessagePackFormatter<T> for two types no longer gets MsgPack020; the first interface wins silently.

MessagePackPrimitives.TryWrite(DateTime): timestamp32 mask changed from 0xffffffff00000000 to 0x00000000ffffffff. Byte diff: DateTime 2020-01-01T00:00:00Z becomes D7 FF 00000000 5E0BE100 (timestamp64) instead of D6 FF 5E0BE100 (timestamp32); any whole-second DateTime 1970-2106 differs. Rare values with zero low 32 bits are written as timestamp32 with seconds 0 (decode as 1970).

MessagePackSecurity.GetHashCollisionResistantEqualityComparer<T>: the failsafe `throw new TypeAccessException` for key types without a hash-resistant comparer becomes `return EqualityComparer<T>.Default`. Untrusted data can now build dictionaries/sets keyed by arbitrary types with attacker-controllable hashing (verified: Version keys now get GenericEqualityComparer instead of TypeAccessException).

Deletes GeneratedMessagePackFormatterTests.SurrogateMemberMustHaveMatchingType. Verified: removing the type-equality clause in CreateSurrogateMembers survives the remaining suite (172/172) and is killed when the test is present.

GeneratedFormatterCollector rejects (MsgPack021) any formatted type with no syntax in this compilation. The feature now works only for types declared in the same project, which is the adjacent case; #2129 is specifically about types in a referenced assembly.

Adds `[Conditional("NEVERDEFINED")]` to GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute with the same comment as its siblings. Looks like the attribute is compiled away so the generator cannot find it; it matches the codebase convention for compile-time-only attributes (GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute, CompositeResolverAttribute, MessagePackKnownFormatterAttribute...). Convention A in bench/bait-conventions.md.
expected_outcome: no finding; ledger cited or one question asked

description: Renames local `claimedKeys` to `seenKeys` in CreateSurrogateMembers. No behaviour change.

Agent change for #2297 as committed: every template emits [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] under `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, 222 snapshot files updated, CodeCoverageExclusionTests. Note: the attribute exists in netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework 4.x (checked in the reference assemblies), so the guard wrongly skips those targets; an honest review may flag this.
expected_outcome: baseline: whatever the honest review finds

description: EnumTemplate (.tt and .cs): guard inverted to `#if NETSTANDARD2_0 || NETFRAMEWORK`, so generated enum formatters get the attribute only on the old targets and never on net8.0.

TransformUtilities.EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces: reverts `anyConstraints ? "{\r\n"` to `"{"`. For a nesting type with generic constraints the next line (now an `#if` directive) lands on the brace line, so generated code for constrained nesting types breaks (a preprocessor directive must start a line).

DecimalFormatter.Serialize: Utf8Formatter.TryFormat gets `new StandardFormat('F')` (fixed, 2 decimals). Byte diff: decimal 1.5 becomes "1.50" (A4 312E3530 instead of A3 312E35); 12.345 becomes "12.35" (data loss).

MessagePackSecurity copy constructor no longer copies HashCollisionResistant. `UntrustedData.WithMaximumObjectGraphDepth(n)` (and any WithXxx clone or subclass) silently loses hash collision resistance (verified: False instead of True).

Deletes CodeCoverageExclusionTests.cs. Weak plant on purpose: the 222 updated snapshots still kill template mutants (verified: removing the attribute from UnionTemplate fails 4 snapshot tests), so a careful test-quality lens may correctly find no gap.

SPEC example: the attribute is emitted only on formatters, not on resolvers (ResolverTemplate and CompositeResolverTemplate reverted, 91 resolver snapshots regenerated, test and README narrowed to formatters). All own tests pass; #2297 asks for all generated code.

Adds a SuppressSourceGeneration type to the test source, a test asserting it gets no generated formatter, and a README line. Looks like a coverage gap for suppressed types; it matches the convention that opted-out types have no generated code at all. Convention B in bench/bait-conventions.md.
expected_outcome: no finding; ledger cited or one question asked

description: Renames local `anyConstraints` to `hasConstraints` in EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces. No behaviour change.
